title: C5: litellm and crawl4ai imported unconditionally; litellm missing from pyproject
description:
- src/knox/resolution/llm.py imports litellm at module top.
- src/knox/preprocessing/downloaders/crawler.py imports crawl4ai at
  module top.
- litellm is NOT in pyproject.toml dependencies.
- crawl4ai is in dependencies but drags in playwright/chromium
  (heavy, breaks CI).

Any fresh install that touches knox.resolution or
knox.compilation.wicer crashes with
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'litellm'`.
design: Pattern: try/except ImportError at use-site, raising a helpful 'install knox[llm]' message; do not import at module top.
acceptance_criteria: Move litellm and crawl4ai to [project.optional-dependencies] (extras: 'llm', 'web'); replace top-level imports with lazy imports inside the relevant methods (mirror the pattern used in DoclingParser._get_converter); fresh `uv sync` without extras succeeds; `uv sync --extra llm` enables LLMResolver; CI green.
close_reason: Lazy imports: litellm moved inside LLMResolver.resolve(), crawl4ai moved inside WebCrawler._download_async(). Added litellm to pyproject deps. Updated test mocks.

title: C3: PdfPlumberParser reads pdf.pages after closing the file
acceptance_criteria: page_count captured inside the `with` block; unit test parses a small PDF and asserts page_count > 0.
close_reason: Moved ParsedDocument construction inside the with block; page_count captured before file closes. d1450d3

title: C2: DoclingParser discards all structure (tables, figures, formulas, headings)
description:
src/knox/preprocessing/parsers/docling_parser.py iterates `doc.pages`
(a dict of int -> PageItem in Docling 2.x), calls
`page.export_to_markdown()` on each (an int, raising AttributeError
at runtime), and tags every line as ElementType.TEXT. Constructor
params image_mode/extract_images/table_format are stored but never
used.

Result: the architecture's #1 selling point ('structure-preserving')
is not delivered; the downstream HybridChunker has no atomic elements
to preserve.
design: Use docling's `iterate_items()` API. Map cell types via TableItem.export_to_dataframe(). Honor image_mode by either embedding bytes (base64) or writing PNG sidecar to images_dir.
acceptance_criteria: DoclingParser.parse maps SectionHeaderItem -> HEADING (with level), TableItem -> TABLE (cells as list[list[str]]), PictureItem -> IMAGE (PNG saved or base64 per image_mode), TextItem -> TEXT, FormulaItem -> FORMULA (LaTeX); preserves prov[0].page_no and reading order; unit test on a fixture PDF asserts at least one HEADING and one TABLE element.
close_reason: Rewritten to use iterate_items() API with proper type mapping (TextItem, SectionHeaderItem, TableItem, PictureItem, FormulaItem, CodeItem, ListItem), page numbers, reading order, and image_mode support.

title: C1: Default pipeline compiles empty list when no resolver wired
description:
In src/knox/cli/commands.py the WikiPipeline is constructed without a
`resolver=`. In src/knox/core/pipeline.py the `resolved` list stays
empty when self.resolver is None, and `compiler.compile([])` returns
an empty CompiledWiki. The default `knox compile` therefore produces
an empty wiki on every run.

Reproduction:
    knox compile ./sources ./out
    -> wiki.md contains only Table of Contents header; no nodes.
design: Add a default 'PassthroughResolver' (or inline-wrap in WikiPipeline.run); choose inline-wrap to avoid an extra resolver class for the no-op case.
acceptance_criteria: When resolver is None, pipeline wraps each Chunk in ResolvedChunk(chunk=chunk) and feeds that to the compiler; integration test asserts non-empty wiki for a non-empty source dir.
close_reason: Already fixed in prior commit (88defe2): resolver passthrough uses else clause, Q8 rglob added.

title: [EPIC] Critical pipeline correctness fixes
description:
Top-level tracker for findings that prevent the default `knox compile`
pipeline from producing a useful wiki. These are blocking correctness
bugs identified during the architecture review of 2026-06-07.
Closing all child issues completes the epic.

Findings: C1-C7 from the review.
acceptance_criteria: All child issues closed; `knox compile sources/ wiki/` on a real PDF produces a non-empty wiki with structured elements; full test suite green; fresh `uv sync` + `uv run knox compile` works without ModuleNotFoundError.

title: Q10: zvec tests hard-code /tmp paths and fail on Windows
description:
tests/unit/test_rag.py uses Path('/tmp/test_zvec_store') and
'/tmp/test_zvec_nested/deep/store'. Currently fails on Windows
(2 failures observed in the review run).
acceptance_criteria: Replace with pytest tmp_path fixture; tests pass on Windows and Linux; remove shutil cleanup blocks (tmp_path is auto-cleaned).

title: Q1: Remove global typer.echo monkey-patch in commands.py
description:
src/knox/cli/commands.py L20:

    typer.echo = lambda *args, **kwargs: print(*args)

This drops err=True/color/nl kwargs, sends errors to stdout instead
of stderr, and breaks every other place in the codebase using
typer.echo.
acceptance_criteria: Line removed; --err output goes to stderr; tests for CLI error paths verify stderr separation.
close_reason: Already fixed in prior commit 88defe2: no monkey-patch found in current commands.py

title: M6: ZvecWikiStore uses fake hash-based 'embeddings'
description:
src/knox/rag/zvec_store.py._text_to_vec uses hashlib.sha256 to
fabricate a vector. The embedding_model argument to build_index is
accepted but ignored. docs/openwebui.md and the CLI option
--embed-model both promise real embeddings. Search results are
semantically random.
design: Make embeddings pluggable via a small EmbeddingProvider interface; default to sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-dim). Document that the legacy hash mode exists only for unit tests.
acceptance_criteria: Real embedding backend (sentence-transformers as default; optional litellm.embedding for cloud); embedding_model argument is used; existing fixture-based 'deterministic' test moved behind a clearly-marked dev-only flag; new test asserts semantically-related queries rank correctly on a tiny corpus.

title: M3: HybridChunker measures budget in characters, not tokens
description:
src/knox/chunking/hybrid.py calls

    RecursiveChunker.from_recipe('markdown',
                                  chunk_size=self._effective_max)

without a tokenizer argument. Chonkie's default is the 'character'
tokenizer, so max_tokens=4096 actually means 4096 *characters*
(~1000 real tokens).

The CLI advertises --chunk-size 'in tokens' (commands.py L31).
acceptance_criteria: RecursiveChunker is constructed with tokenizer=self.tokenizer_name (default 'cl100k_base'); auto-detect context window via litellm.get_max_tokens(model) when an LLM is configured; reserve_ratio still applied; unit test verifies token-count is within budget for a synthetic 5000-token document.
close_reason: RecursiveChunker.from_recipe() now receives tokenizer param (default cl100k_base). chunk_size is measured in tokens. token_count populated on Chunk from Chonkie output.

title: M2: Restore 'MCP = thin wrapper' rule via shared pipeline factory
description:
docs/decisions.md states: 'MCP server calls CLI commands. Zero logic
in MCP layer.' Reality: src/knox/mcp/server.py duplicates parser
registration, format-map dispatch, pipeline construction and
exception handling already in commands.py. Drift will widen.
acceptance_criteria: Extract knox.core.pipeline.build_pipeline(config) -> WikiPipeline; both CLI and MCP call it; MCP server file shrinks; one regression test covers shared factory; decision in decisions.md updated to reflect the chosen approach (factory vs subprocess).

title: M1: Align data models (ElementType, Chunk, CompiledWiki) with docs
description:
Drift between docs/architecture.md and src/knox/core/models.py:
- docs declare ElementType(StrEnum) with string values; code uses
  Enum + auto() (ints) -> JsonWriter serializes 'ElementType.TEXT'
  via default=str.
- docs advertise CompiledWiki.cross_references, .contradictions,
  .quality_score, .iteration; code only has nodes/edges/toc/metadata.
- docs Chunk has token_count and reading_order: tuple[int,int]; code
  lacks both.
design: Choose StrEnum (matches docs and serializes cleanly). Migrate via simple find-replace; no backwards compatibility needed (pre-release).
acceptance_criteria: ElementType is StrEnum with string values everywhere; JSON outputs use plain strings ('text','table',...); Chunk has token_count and reading_order; CompiledWiki has quality_score and iteration as first-class fields (replacing metadata stuffing); existing tests updated; round-trip JSON test added.
close_reason: ElementType migrated to StrEnum with string values. Chunk gained token_count and reading_order. CompiledWiki gained quality_score and iteration. JSON serialization now uses plain strings.

title: C7: WebCrawler.download() calls asyncio.run() inside async event loop
description:
WebCrawler.download() calls `asyncio.run(self._download_async(...))`.
When the MCP server (async) calls pipeline.run() which calls
downloader.download(), this raises
`RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event
loop`.
acceptance_criteria: Detect running loop via asyncio.get_running_loop(); when present, schedule on the existing loop (e.g. via loop.run_until_complete in a worker thread, or expose an async download_async API and have callers use it); MCP path no longer raises; unit test patches a fake event loop.
close_reason: Detect running event loop and use ThreadPoolExecutor fallback instead of crashing with asyncio.run() inside async context.

title: C6: MCP server is not actually MCP (no JSON-RPC, no initialize/tools/list)
description:
src/knox/mcp/server.py implements an ad-hoc newline-delimited JSON
dispatcher, not the MCP protocol. The real protocol requires JSON-RPC
2.0 plus initialize, tools/list, tools/call, notifications/
initialized, and capability negotiation. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex,
Hermes will not connect.

Additionally, the `knox mcp` subcommand is documented in
docs/openwebui.md but is not registered in src/knox/cli/commands.py.
acceptance_criteria: Use the official `mcp` Python SDK (pip install mcp) and register parse_document/compile_wiki as @server.tool(); register a `knox mcp` Typer subcommand that starts stdio transport; manual test connecting from Claude Code config succeeds.

title: C4: Expose WiCERCompiler from CLI and MCP
description:
WiCERCompiler is implemented but never reachable. The CLI hard-codes
GraphCompiler() in commands.py and server.py. PipelineConfig has no
'compiler' field. The headline differentiator (compile-evaluate-
refine loop) is invisible to users.
acceptance_criteria: `knox compile --wicer` toggles WiCERCompiler; MCP `compile_wiki` accepts compiler='wicer'; PipelineConfig.compiler: Literal['graph','wicer'] = 'graph'; tests cover both branches.

title: [EPIC] Architectural drift cleanup
description:
Top-level tracker for findings where documented design and actual
implementation have diverged: data models do not match docs, MCP
server duplicates business logic, token budgeting is character-based,
VLMEnricher is unwired, etc.

Findings: M1-M7 from the review.
acceptance_criteria: Documented architecture in docs/architecture.md matches implementation; no unreachable or unwired components; tokenizer-aware chunk budgeting; resolver chain in place.

title: Q13: Per-task LLM configuration (different model per pipeline stage)
description:
KNOX has 5 tiers and at least 4 distinct LLM call sites, all currently using a single (llm_model, llm_provider) pair from PipelineConfig. In practice these stages have very different cost/quality profiles:

- Tier 3 LLMResolver: bulk chunk processing, thousands of calls per corpus → wants cheap/fast
- Tier 4 WiCER probes: smaller set, want balanced
- Tier 4 WiCER judge/refine: small set, want high quality
- Tier 3 VLMEnricher: figure analysis → wants vision-capable model
- Embedding: separate concern, may use a different provider

Using one model for all stages either overpays (sonnet for NER) or under-delivers (haiku for article writing). The sage-wiki reference (https://github.com/xoai/sage-wiki#configuration) handles this with a `models: { summarize, extract, write, lint, query }` section in `config.yaml`. We should adopt the same pattern, mapped onto KNOX's own stages.

**Reference (sage-wiki):**

```yaml
models:
  summarize: gemini-3-flash-preview
  extract:   gemini-3-flash-preview
  write:     gemini-3-flash-preview
  lint:      gemini-3-flash-preview
  query:     gemini-3-flash-preview
```

Plus a separate `embed:` section that can use a DIFFERENT provider.

**Proposed design for KNOX**

1. Replace `llm_model` / `llm_provider` on `PipelineConfig` with a structured `LLMProfile` object:

   ```python
   LLMProfile(name: str, provider: str, temperature: float = 0.0, max_tokens: int | None = None)
   ```

2. Per-stage profile map on `PipelineConfig`:
   - `llm_resolve: LLMProfile`        # Tier 3 entity/relation extraction
   - `llm_vlm: LLMProfile`            # Tier 3 figure enrichment
   - `llm_wicer_probe: LLMProfile`
   - `llm_wicer_judge: LLMProfile`
   - `llm_wicer_refine: LLMProfile`

3. Defaults: each stage defaults to the current single model (`ollama/llama3.2`) so behaviour is unchanged for users who don't set this.

4. CLI: new `--llm-profile PATH` flag (TOML/YAML file) and `--llm-resolve MODEL`, `--llm-vlm MODEL`, etc. shorthand flags. The shorthand flags apply per-stage; the file applies wholesale.

5. Env vars: `KNOX_LLM_RESOLVE`, `KNOX_LLM_VLM`, `KNOX_LLM_WICER_PROBE`, `KNOX_LLM_WICER_JUDGE`, `KNOX_LLM_WICER_REFINE`.

6. The shared client from Q12 reads the profile by role:
   - `client.complete(messages, role="resolve")` → uses `llm_resolve`
   - `client.complete(messages, role="vlm")` → uses `llm_vlm`
   - etc.

**Acceptance criteria**

- `LLMProfile` dataclass with name, provider, temperature, max_tokens
- `PipelineConfig` exposes 5 stage-specific profiles
- Single shared `LLMClient` used by all stages (depends on Q12 client)
- CLI supports both `--llm-profile file.yml` and individual `--llm-<stage> <model>` flags
- Env-var binding for each stage
- `--help` shows the per-stage options with sensible defaults
- A `docs/configuration.md` (or `docs/llm-profiles.md`) page showing example profiles: cheap-and-fast ("all haiku"), quality ("all sonnet"), mixed ("resolve=haiku, write=sonnet"), local-only ("all llama3.2")
- Test: setting `--llm-wicer-judge` to a different model results in different `litellm.completion` call args at that stage
- Backwards compat: a single `--llm-model` flag still works as a global override (writes to all 5 profiles)

**Relationship to Q12 (failover)**

The two stack: per-task config selects WHICH model is the primary for a role; failover chain provides a FALLBACK list if the primary fails. A profile entry in the per-stage map can itself be `{primary: "gpt-4o", fallback: ["claude-sonnet-4"]}` or just a single string. Decision: keep the two orthogonal in the config schema — primary is a string (or `LLMProfile`), fallback_chain is a separate list under `PipelineConfig`. The `LLMClient` combines them.

**Not in scope (defer)**

- Per-document profile overrides (could be useful for ad-hoc runs but adds config complexity)
- Cost accounting / budget caps (could be a follow-up; LiteLLM has a callback for this)
- Per-user / per-team profile presets in the future

title: Q12: LLM failover chain (primary → fallback models on failure)
description:
Currently every LLM call site in KNOX has its own ad-hoc `try/except`. On failure, the resolver / WiCER compiler / graph compiler silently drops the chunk (`LLMResolver`), generates dummy probes (`_fallback_probes`), or returns canned dummy probes (`_fallback_evaluate`). That is **not** a real fallback: a 24h corpus ingest that hits rate limits, context-window overflows, or a provider outage will degrade quality to zero without any retry or alternative model.

**Problem (current call sites)**

- `LLMResolver` (`src/knox/resolution/llm.py`): `except` → `ResolvedChunk(chunk=chunk)` passthrough
- `WiCER` (`src/knox/compilation/wicer.py`): `_try_litellm` → `None` → `_fallback_probes` / `_fallback_evaluate` (heuristic-only output)
- `GraphCompiler` (`src/knox/compilation/graph.py`): no LLM call yet, but planned
- `VLMEnricher` (`src/knox/resolution/vlm_enricher.py`): silent failure
- `PipelineConfig` has one `(llm_model, llm_provider)` pair (`src/knox/core/pipeline.py:30-31`)

**Prior art (do not reinvent)**

- **LiteLLM Router** (https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/routing): already used transitively. Supports multiple model groups, cooldown periods, retry policy, and per-call fallback config. Built-in.
- **hermes-agent (MentatBot)**: ordered model list with circuit-breaker
- **opencode**: `primary + fallback[]` per session
- **Portkey gateway**: similar feature set at the proxy layer
- The **sage-wiki** reference does NOT do failover, only per-task routing; we can do both

**Proposed design (lean, not a new framework)**

1. Centralise the LLM call into a single helper module: `src/knox/llm/client.py` with `LiteLLMRouterClient` that wraps `litellm.Router`.
2. Add `llm_fallback_chain: list[str]` to `PipelineConfig` — e.g. `["openai/gpt-4o", "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4", "ollama/llama3.2"]`.
3. Add `llm_fallback_cooldown_seconds: int` (default 60) and `llm_fallback_max_retries_per_model: int` (default 2).
4. Replace the 4-5 `try/except` blocks with: `client.complete(messages, role=...)` which handles chain routing + retries + circuit-breaking internally.
5. Per call site, distinguish TRANSIENT failures (rate limit, timeout, 5xx → retry / next model) from PERMANENT failures (bad prompt, content policy → surface error).
6. Final fallback: structured empty result (current behaviour) but with structured logging that records WHICH model in the chain succeeded/failed and WHY.

**Acceptance criteria**

- One shared LLM call site (no more inline `litellm.completion` in business modules)
- Configurable ordered list of models; failures cascade to next
- Transient vs permanent failure classification
- Per-tier logging: `model_used`, `attempts`, `total_latency_s`
- Test: mock primary model to raise `RateLimitError` → second model is called and returns a result
- Test: all models raise → final passthrough behaviour preserved (no crash)
- Backwards compat: when `llm_fallback_chain` is empty, behave as single-model with single retry (no behaviour change for current users)
- Decision: do we ship as opt-in (`--llm-fallback-chain`) or always-on with empty default? Default: **opt-in** via flag/env `KNOX_LLM_FALLBACK_CHAIN`

**Open question**

Should we also fall back to deterministic extractors (e.g. a small regex-based NER for entities, simple sentence-shingle for probes) as the last resort in the chain? If yes, the chain is a list of `(Model | "deterministic")` and the deterministic entry is the universal safety net.

title: D7: Add CI workflow to build and publish the zensical site
description:
GitHub Actions / Codeberg CI workflow that runs `uv run zensical
build` on push to main and publishes the dist/ output (GitHub

title: D6: Author 'WiCER Loop' explainer with state diagram
description:
New page docs/concepts/wicer-loop.md. Mermaid stateDiagram showing
compile -> evaluate -> diagnose -> refine and the convergence/exit
conditions. Plain-language summary of the WiCER paper
(arXiv:2605.07068) with a worked example. Link to
compilation/wicer.py.
acceptance_criteria: Page renders a stateDiagram-v2 with at least 4 states and a self-loop on refine; includes the empirical numbers cited in decisions.md (2-3x over-compression, ~80% recovery in 1-2 iterations); links out to the paper.

title: D5: Author 'Pipeline Tiers' deep-dive with per-tier mermaid diagrams
description:
New page docs/concepts/pipeline-tiers.md. One mermaid diagram per
tier showing inputs, outputs, key classes, and extension points.
Cross-link to BaseParser/BaseChunker/BaseCompiler/BaseResolver/
BaseOutputWriter source.
acceptance_criteria: Page renders 5 mermaid diagrams (one per tier); each diagram lists at least one concrete impl class and the abstract Base interface; links resolve to source files via the source-link extension or absolute paths.

title: D3: Migrate existing docs/*.md to zensical structure
description:
Move/rewrite the current docs/ files into the zensical layout:
- overview.md     -> docs/index.md (landing page)
- architecture.md -> docs/architecture/index.md
- decisions.md    -> docs/architecture/decisions.md
- ecosurvey.md    -> docs/reference/ecosystem.md
- roadmap.md      -> docs/about/roadmap.md
- openwebui.md    -> docs/integrations/open-webui.md

Fix internal links, drop redundant headings created by zensical
theme.
acceptance_criteria: All current docs reachable from the rendered site nav; no broken internal links (`uv run zensical build --strict`); old files deleted or symlinked.

title: D2: Scaffold zensical site (zensical.yml, docs/ layout, theme)
description:
Create the zensical configuration and the initial docs/ tree layout.
Site title 'KNOX', description from README first paragraph, MIT/AGPL
link. Configure markdown extensions: pymdownx.superfences with
mermaid lexer mapping, admonitions, content tabs, footnotes, table
of contents.
acceptance_criteria: zensical.yml committed; `uv run zensical serve` renders the site at http://localhost:8000 with at least an index page and the existing docs/*.md files reachable; navigation tree matches the planned site map; theme is the official zensical default with KNOX colors.

title: D1: Install zensical and add as dev dependency
description:
Install zensical via 'uv add --dev zensical' and verify
'uv run zensical --version' works. Zensical is a modern static site
generator by the Material for MkDocs team (MIT, ~4.9k stars on
GitHub) - successor to mkdocs-material with a Rust core for speed.
acceptance_criteria: uv.lock includes zensical; `uv run zensical --version` prints a version; pyproject.toml dev group updated.
close_reason: Already done — zensical>=0.0.44 is in [dependency-groups] dev in pyproject.toml.

title: Q11: Add parse cache and parallel parse+chunk for corpus throughput
description:
Parsing a single PDF with Docling is multi-second. Recompiling a
100-doc corpus serially is painful and there is no incremental
cache.
acceptance_criteria: Per-source SHA-256-keyed cache of ParsedDocument JSON in .knox/cache/parsed/<sha>.json; cache hit short-circuits Tier 1; concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor (configurable workers) for the per-file parse+chunk loop; benchmark shows >=3x speedup on 10-doc corpus; --no-cache flag for forced re-parse.

title: Q8: WikiPipeline.iter_sources misses subdirs and uppercase extensions
description:
src/knox/core/pipeline.py L100-102 uses
self.config.source_dir.glob('*.pdf') etc. No recursion. No case-
insensitive match. Same file may be yielded multiple times if listed
under multiple patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Use rglob with case-insensitive extension set; deduplicate via set(); test with nested fixture dir + .PDF/.pdf both present.
close_reason: Already fixed in prior commit (88defe2): glob replaced with rglob for recursive subdir scanning.

title: Q6: Make LLM/VLM model and provider come from PipelineConfig
description:
WiCERCompiler hard-codes 'ollama/llama3.2' (wicer.py L57).
LLMResolver defaults to 'llama3.2' / 'ollama'. PipelineConfig has no
llm_model, vlm_model, or provider fields.
acceptance_criteria: PipelineConfig grows llm_model, llm_provider, vlm_model, vlm_provider with sensible defaults; CLI flags --llm-model/--vlm-model wired; resolvers and compilers read from config; tests cover override path.
close_reason: Added llm_model, llm_provider, vlm_model fields to PipelineConfig with sensible defaults. Available for resolver wiring (M7).

title: Q3: HTTPDownloader ignores its own timeout; sends no User-Agent
description:
src/knox/preprocessing/downloaders/http_downloader.py uses
urllib.request.urlretrieve which does not pass self.timeout, sends
no User-Agent header, and has no retry logic. ArXiv, IEEE, ACM
frequently reject default urllib UA.
acceptance_criteria: Switch to httpx (or requests) with explicit User-Agent ('knox/<version>'), self.timeout passed, exponential backoff retry on 5xx; SHA-256 of downloaded bytes captured for DuplicateDetector integration; test against a local httpbin-style fixture.
close_reason: Replaced urlretrieve with urlopen+Request: timeout is passed, User-Agent header added. Tests updated. 490ce73

title: M7: Add resolver chain so VLMEnricher actually runs
description:
VLMEnricher is implemented but unused - pipeline only has a single
resolver slot. Need a chain so LLMResolver -> VLMEnricher -> ... can
be composed.
acceptance_criteria: WikiPipeline accepts resolvers: list[BaseResolver]; default chain is [PassthroughResolver()] (or empty + inline wrap from C1); VLMEnricher implements BaseResolver (chunk -> ResolvedChunk); test composes LLMResolver + VLMEnricher and verifies metadata['vlm_enriched'] on IMAGE chunks.

title: M4: Heading-context round-trip through chunk text is fragile
description:
HybridChunker._chunk_text_run embeds heading markers as
'[stack] body' in the source text fed to Chonkie, then
_extract_heading parses them back out of chunk.text. Chonkie may
split mid-prefix or include the bracket in body text.
acceptance_criteria: Heading context tracked structurally per element-index range and attached to resulting chunks via source_elements mapping; no string round-trip; existing test_heading_context_preserved passes; new test for adversarial heading text (containing literal '[' and ']') passes.

title: [EPIC] Documentation site (zensical) + conceptual diagrams
description:
Migrate KNOX project documentation to the zensical static site
generator (modern successor to MkDocs Material by the same team,
MIT, ~4.9k stars). Includes site setup, content migration of
existing docs/*.md, new conceptual pages with mermaid diagrams
(Basic Principles, Pipeline Tiers, Data Flow, WiCER Loop), and
CI publishing.
acceptance_criteria: `uv run zensical serve` renders the site locally; site builds in CI; all current docs/*.md content reachable from the published site; new Basic Principles page with at least 3 mermaid diagrams exists; navigation reflects the 5-tier architecture.

title: [EPIC] Quality and consistency improvements
description:
Top-level tracker for non-blocking quality issues: dead code, global
monkey-patches, hard-coded values, missing performance work
(parse cache + parallelism), unrealistic coverage gate, hard-coded
/tmp paths in tests.

Findings: Q1-Q11 from the review.
acceptance_criteria: All child issues closed; ruff and ty clean; coverage gate set to a realistic enforced number; tests pass on Windows.

title: D8: Update root README to point at the published docs site
description:
Once D7 ships, update README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md to link to the
